title: Kaleidohedra by DICTO: shearable lattices, new space-fillers and the Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli (EKP) cell
description:
Kaleidohedra by DICTO: working notes, verification scripts and a browser app for lattices and the polyhedra on them. This snapshot records finding #12 of DISCOVERIES.md, the Star Chain Reaction, and its study 12a, the Dragon chain, first recorded 2026-10-08.

All Kaleidohedra findings (DISCOVERIES.md; each checked by a script in CI; credit DICTO unless noted):

  1. DICTO skewed rhombic dodecahedron: a rhombic-dodecahedron-type space-filler whose four equal edge directions meet at 60° three times and 72° three times (60° and 72° rhombi), tiling as a sheared FCC. Not found in the literature: candidate.
  2. Equal-edge rule for sheared FCC (Kaleidohedra): the equal-edge cell of every sheared FCC lattice, by a circumcentre shift. General idea known; this form not found.
  3. Bain disphenoids become regular tetrahedra (known, Bain 1924).
  4. Bain rhombic dodecahedron: 4 squares and 8 rhombi of 60° (known).
  5. Regular-hexagon elongated dodecahedron: 4 regular hexagons, 4 squares and 4 rhombi of 60°, all edges equal, filling space by translation; Kaleidohedra's symbol. Known (the truncated octahedron with one zone removed; Grünbaum 2010, Fig. 2b); DICTO reached it independently by a new route, the Bain stretch.
  6. Exactly nine "most regular" space-fillers (Kaleidohedra two-way search): every equal-edge space-filling zonohedron whose faces are only squares, regular hexagons and 60° rhombi.
  7. DICTO skewed elongated dodecahedra (two forms), extending #1.
  8. Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli (EKP) cell, and 8b, the Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli network (below).
  9. Rhombic dodecahedron sub-family (Kaleidohedra, verified by building in Polyhedraverse): 24 sheared-FCC cells from TARGETS.md. Candidates.
  10. EKP windows: carving the six face-neighbours' stella octangulas out of the EKP cell's dodecahedron leaves exactly 12 Penrose thick rhombi (72° and 108°, edge 2/φ), one on each cube edge, each still in the dodecahedron's own face plane; 48 triangles wall the cut-away, the volume is exactly 12, and each of the six roofs keeps exactly 1/φ of itself. An aperiodic tile, at its icosahedral orientation, on a periodic cubic lattice. Not found (web-level search): candidate.
  11. Stretched dodecahedron: the dodecahedron stretched along a cube-face axis has 8 regular pentagons, 4 hexagons (108° four times, 144° twice) and 2 rectangles at any stretch, squares at a stretch of one edge; at the lattice spacing it is the hull of two face-neighbour dodecahedra. Not found (web-level search): candidate.
  12. Studies of #10 (constructions on the windows, not separate claims). 10a, the windows made convex (recorded as #12 in v2026.10.08-convex): pushing the 12 window rhombi straight out by √(7 − 4φ), keeping their size and orientation, the convex hull has 74 faces: 12 Penrose thick rhombi, 6 golden rhombi (diagonals in ratio φ) square on the cube faces, 8 equilateral triangles and 48 triangles, with only three edge lengths. The 2D and 3D aperiodic rhombi together on cubic symmetry. It unfolds into a flat net with no overlaps, so it can be built. 10b, windows and stellas in a checkerboard: the windows (even cells) and stella octangulas (odd cells) fill space exactly, each odd cube being its stella plus its six neighbours' carved roofs (each roof keeps 2/3; volumes 12 + 4 = two cubes): the stella octangula is the windows' other half. The closest prior system found (Lalvani, US 4,723,382) requires all edges on the icosahedral two-fold axes; the stella's and most wall edges are not.
  13. Star Chain Reaction (DICTO's name). Regular dodecahedra in their densest lattice packing leave one hole per cell, a Dogstar (DICTO's name; the solid itself is George W. Hart's stellation 8 of the dodecahedron, 1996, which he noted fills space alternated with regular dodecahedra). It is a partial stellation of a dodecahedron 1/φ³ the size, volume exactly φ/2 at dodecahedron edge 1. New: the EKP cell's great star is exactly the great stellated dodecahedron of that 1/φ³ core, and a whole Sunstar (a dodecahedron with the 6 Dogstars on its faces) 1/φ³ the size fits inside it with no room to grow, so dodecahedron ⊃ great star ⊃ Sunstar(1/φ³) ⊃ great star(1/φ³) ⊃ … nests forever, each step touching, ratio φ³ (the inflation factor of icosahedral quasicrystals). 12a, the Dragon chain: Dragon Jewel (the windows solid, #10) ⊃ cube ⊃ stella octangula ⊃ Dogstar ⊃ dodecahedron(1/φ³) ⊃ Dragon Jewel(1/φ³) ⊃ …, every step touching: the EKP cell recurs inside its own stella. Not found in a web-level search (2026-10-08): candidate.

Also TARGETS.md and geometry-targets.json: the 160 equal-edge space-filling cells whose edge directions meet only at special angles, found by an exact search both ways.

Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli cell. Euclid's roofs on a cube of edge 2 make the regular dodecahedron; reflecting the 12 roof vertices back through the cube faces makes the regular icosahedron. Cube, dodecahedron and icosahedron edges are φ² : φ : 1, and every roof vertex is a vertex of a neighbouring cell's icosahedron. Repeated on a simple cubic lattice: 13 nodes per cell, space group Pm-3 (No. 200), nodes on Wyckoff 1b and 12j with y = 1/(2φ), z = 1/(2φ²). Every cell carries the icosahedron's 31 rotation axes, parallel throughout the crystal; 7 of them are crystal symmetries, and m-3 is exactly the cube's symmetries that are also the icosahedron's. The cell also contains Kepler's great stellated dodecahedron (the icosahedron with 20 golden-triangle spikes reaching the dodecahedron's vertices).

All five Platonic solids in one cell. The six neighbours' roof ridges meet inside each cube as Pacioli's three interlocking golden rectangles, whose corners are the icosahedron. The icosahedron's vertices lie on the edges of the octahedron on the cube-face centres at the golden section; that octahedron is the overlap of Kepler's stella octangula (two regular tetrahedra on alternate cube corners). So icosahedron ⊂ octahedron ⊂ tetrahedra ⊂ cube ⊂ dodecahedron nest exactly in one cell.

Euclid–Kepler–Pacioli network. Great stellated dodecahedra on the even cells (an FCC lattice) and icosahedra on the odd cells share only corners: each star's 12 roof tips are vertices of the six neighbouring icosahedra, with no overlap (exact separating-axis test). Dodecahedra on the even cells alone form the known optimal lattice packing of the regular dodecahedron, density (5+√5)/8.

Every claim is checked numerically by scripts/verify-roof-fold.mjs on each push. A web-level literature search (2026-10-06, recorded in DISCOVERIES.md) did not find the cell or the network; the individual solids, Euclid's construction and the optimal packing are classical. Names chosen by DICTO.
